Jana Kane https://www.litefinance.org/blog/authors/jana-kane/ Silver (XAG/INR) is at ₹3,945.796 per troy ounce as of 20.11.2026, -12.35% against the same day a year ago. This page gives our silver price prediction for India month by month for 2026–2028, silver price predictions for the next 5 years and for 2030, the silver price history in India and the factors that push the local rate up or down. It also covers the short term: whether the silver rate may increase or decrease in the coming days.
 The article covers the following subjects:

 Major Takeaways (as of November 2026)
 Price now : XAG/INR trades at ₹3,945.796 per troy ounce. Multiply by 32.15 to get the cost of 1 kg of 999 fine silver.
 Record : the highest XAG/INR level so far is ₹11,195.402, reached on 29.01.2026.
 Rest of 2026: our model sees silver in India trading from ₹2,455.932 to ₹5,345.230 per troy ounce.
 Coming days : the daily technical signal for XAG/INR is Strong buy, and the model's range for the current month is ₹3,835.482–₹5,057.051 per troy ounce.
 Five-year range : ₹3,118.267–₹4,457.853 per troy ounce.
 What matters most locally : industrial buying, with India's solar factories at the front. The country brings in most of its silver from abroad, so every dip in the rupee raises the price too.
 Silver Real-Time Market Overview (XAG/INR)
 XAG/INR is quoted at ₹3,945.796 per troy ounce right now. Over the last 24 hours it has moved -1.64%, and over the last month -28.35%. The XAG to INR rate rests on two numbers: the dollar price of silver, $42.385 per ounce at the moment, and the USD/INR exchange rate. In India, silver is usually priced per kg or per 10 grams. One kilogram holds 32.15 troy ounces, so multiply the quote by 32.15 for a kilogram or divide it by 3.11 for 10 grams (by 31.1 for the price per gram), taxes not included.
 MCX silver and the IBJA rate come out higher than this conversion because duties are added on top. From May 13, 2026, imported silver pays 15% (a 10% basic customs duty and a 5% AIDC), followed by 3% GST. You do not need bars or coins to trade these moves: on LiteFinance, you open a position on the XAG/INR price itself, whether you expect it to rise or fall.
 Will the Silver Rate Increase or Decrease in the Coming Days in India?
 Over a few days, silver moves on news and on trader positioning far more than on solar demand or import duty. So for the coming days we show live readings that refresh daily. Right now XAG/INR looks like this:
 Daily technical signal : Strong buy.
 Support : ₹3,881.435. Buyers tend to step in around these levels when the price slips.
 Resistance : ₹5,973.916. A rise needs to clear these levels to continue.
 Weekly direction by Ichimoku : downward.
 Trader positioning : 66.21% of LiteFinance traders hold positions in the direction: Sell.
 The chart shows the path the model draws for the next 7 days.
 Will the silver rate decrease in the coming days?
 Silver in rupees usually gives ground in three cases: the US dollar strengthens and metals fall worldwide, the rupee gains against the dollar, or weak factory data raises doubts about industrial orders. Silver also tends to fall harder than gold on the same news, because its market is smaller. Over the past month XAG/INR has changed by -28.35%, and the record is 183.73% above the current price. If the decline continues, the first reference points are the support levels above, then the model's low for the current month, ₹3,835.482 per troy ounce.
 Will the silver rate increase in the coming days?
 A rise is more likely when the Fed signals lower rates, when the rupee weakens, or when dealers restock ahead of Dhanteras, Diwali and the wedding season. The model's upper bound is ₹5,057.051 for the current month and ₹5,345.230 for the rest of 2026. To turn any of these figures into the silver price per kg, multiply by 32.15.
 Silver Price Forecast for 2026 in India
 The first table holds our silver price prediction for 2026 in India for the months left in the year. Each row gives the projected low, average and high for XAG/INR in that month, priced per troy ounce.
 Date Minimum, ₹ Average Price, ₹ Maximum, ₹ 
 15.12.2026 2,455.932 3,778.825 5,345.230 
 Until December, our silver rate prediction for 2026 in India keeps XAG/INR within ₹2,455.932–₹5,345.230, averaging ₹3,949.255. For the full calendar year, the expected price change comes to -41.74%.
 Late autumn and winter are peak buying months. Families buy silver coins, utensils and jewellery for Dhanteras and Diwali, and orders stay strong while the wedding season lasts. Supply has become harder to secure: bar imports have required government approval since May 2026, which keeps Indian quotes at a premium to the converted world price.
 Highest Silver Rate in 2026 in India
 The highest silver rate on record for XAG/INR is ₹11,195.402, set on 29.01.2026. Multiply it by 32.15 for the price of 1 kg, or divide it by 31.1 for the price per gram, before duty and GST. That peak is 183.73% above the current rate. For the months left in 2026, the model's highest level is ₹5,345.230 and its lowest is ₹2,455.932 per troy ounce.

 Early February brings the Union Budget, where the government tends to revise customs duty and GST on precious metals. A duty change reaches Indian silver prices within days. Unlike gold, silver also depends on factory orders: solar panel producers need silver paste month after month, so new solar capacity sets a steady base for demand. Decisions by the Fed and the RBI shift the US dollar and the Indian rupee, and silver usually swings more than gold when they do.

 The biggest long-term driver is solar power. India aims for 500 GW of non-fossil power capacity by 2030, solar is expected to supply the largest share, and each panel uses silver. At the same time, producers keep reducing the silver content per panel, which slows this demand. Silver ETFs, open to Indian investors since 2022, tie investment buying more to price moves than to the festival calendar. Meanwhile, the rupee's gradual weakening against the dollar keeps lifting local prices.

 From 2027 to 2031, the future silver rate in India is expected to stay in the ₹3,118.267–₹4,457.853 corridor, with a price target of about ₹3,720.026 for the end of 2031. To get the silver price per kg for any year, multiply the figure in the table by 32.15.
 Will the silver price increase? Compare the current ₹3,945.796 with the level the model expects at the end of 2031. Either way, the route will not be smooth. Volatility in silver is higher than in gold: in 2025, its dollar price jumped about 144%, the strongest year since 1979, and falls can be just as steep. The main things to follow are solar and electronics demand, the Fed and the dollar, and the USD/INR rate.
 Silver Price Prediction 2030 in India and Long-Term Outlook to 2035
 For the silver price prediction 2030 in India, the model gives a range of ₹3,188.863–₹4,431.386 per troy ounce. Multiply by 32.15 to estimate the 1 kg silver price in 2030 in India. For 2035, the range widens to ₹3,291.614–₹4,556.522.
 A forecast that reaches into the 2030s carries a lot of uncertainty, so here are three ways the silver rate in 2030 in India could turn out:
 Bullish : the global market stays short of silver because of solar and electronics, inflation does not ease, and the rupee loses more ground. XAG/INR approaches the upper end of the range.
 Base : industry buys more silver each year but uses less per panel, and silver gains about as much as inflation plus the rupee's decline. XAG/INR hovers around the middle.
 Bearish : higher real rates and a stronger dollar weigh on precious metals, and manufacturers switch some silver to copper. XAG/INR slides toward the lower end, with the weaker rupee cushioning the fall for Indian buyers.
 What Drives Silver Prices in India
 World prices set the starting point, and Indian conditions add the rest. These five factors carry the most weight:
 The rupee. India produces little silver of its own and covers most of its needs with imports, so a weaker rupee lifts the local price even when XAG/USD does not move.
 Industrial demand. Solar panels, electronics and electric vehicles all use silver. By April 2026, India had about 154 GW of solar capacity installed, and the plan is roughly 300 GW by 2030, which means steadily growing orders for silver paste.
 Duties and import rules. A 15% import duty has applied since May 13, 2026, plus 3% GST. Three days later, bars of 99.9% silver moved to the restricted list, and importers now need approval from the  Directorate General of Foreign Trade .
 Festivals and weddings. Coins, utensils and jewellery sell fastest around Dhanteras, Diwali and the wedding season, and dealers raise premiums as they stock up beforehand.
 The Fed and the world market. Every Fed rate decision moves the US dollar and precious metals with it. While the Fed rate stands at +3.88% and XAG/USD trades at $42.385, each meeting can change the outlook for Indian silver. Traders also look at the gold/silver ratio: a reading that is high by historical standards is often taken as a hint that silver is undervalued against gold.

 XAG/INR reached its all-time high of ₹11,195.402 on 29.01.2026. Its lowest recorded level, ₹46.844, dates from 21.06.1982.
 In nine years, silver in India went from an average of about ₹37,000 to over ₹112,000 per kg, roughly 13% a year. Three years (2017, 2018 and 2022) ended lower, and 2025 by itself added 47.5%.
 Forecasting Methodology
 We build the XAG/INR forecast from two separate projections: silver in US dollars (XAG/USD) and the USD/INR exchange rate. Their product gives the expected rupee price per troy ounce. Import duty (15%) and GST (3%) are not included, so shop prices in India will be higher.

 Silver Rate Prediction in India: FAQ
 Will the silver rate decrease in India? For a while, yes, that is possible, and silver usually drops faster than gold. A stronger rupee, a Fed that holds rates high, weaker industrial orders or a duty cut could all push the Indian price lower. Our model already includes such dips: its lowest point for 2027 is ₹3,118.267 per troy ounce.
 What will be the silver rate in India in the next 5 years? Our silver rate prediction for the next 5 years in India keeps XAG/INR in the ₹3,118.267–₹4,457.853 band per troy ounce, with the price ending up around ₹3,720.026 at the end of 2031. Multiply by 32.15 to convert to the price per kg.
 Is it a good time to buy silver in India now? It depends on why you are buying. Short-term traders can check the daily signal, currently Strong buy, while support sits at ₹3,881.435 and resistance at ₹5,973.916. If you are investing for years, buying in several parts usually works better than guessing the lowest point, especially with a metal that swings as much as silver.
 Why is silver more expensive in India than the international price? Most silver sold in India is imported. Importers pay the dollar price converted into rupees plus a 15% customs duty, and buyers then pay 3% GST. Bar imports have needed government approval since May 2026, which keeps supply tight. Jewellery and utensils carry making charges as well, and those attract 5% GST.
 Will the silver rate decrease in the coming days in India? The daily signal for XAG/INR is Strong buy, with support at ₹3,881.435. A decline is more likely when the US dollar or the rupee strengthens, or when industrial demand looks weak. The model's low for the current month is ₹3,835.482 per troy ounce.
 Will the silver rate increase in the coming days in India? Resistance for XAG/INR sits at ₹5,973.916, and the daily signal is Strong buy. Silver tends to rise when the Fed moves toward lower rates, the rupee weakens or festival buying picks up. The model's high for the current month is ₹5,057.051 per troy ounce.
 What is the highest silver rate in 2026 in India? The record for XAG/INR is ₹11,195.402 per troy ounce, reached on 29.01.2026. Multiply by 32.15 to get the price per kg. For the rest of 2026, the model's maximum is ₹5,345.230.
 When will silver prices go up in India? Silver in rupees usually goes up when the Fed cuts rates, the rupee weakens against the dollar or industrial buyers increase orders. The model's upper bound is ₹5,345.230 for the rest of 2026 and ₹4,322.990 for 2027.
